newsitem.title: ITALY: FOCUS - Inflation in Italy hits 27-year low.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Inflation in Italy hits 27-year low.

text.p: Inflation in Italy fell to its lowest for 27 years in November, according to figures released on Thursday which analysts said underscored expectations of a further cut in interest rates before the end of the month.
The national statistics office ISTAT said consumer price inflation last month was 2.6 percent year-on-year, down from 3.0 percent in October and 6.0 percent in November 1995.
It was the lowest since June 1969, when the figure was 2.5 percent, and confirmed recent provisional data released by 10 sample cities.
The monthly consumer price inflation (CPI) index rose 0.3 percent in November, compared with a rise of 0.1 percent in October and 0.6 percent in November 1995, ISTAT said.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi, whose centre-left government took office in May, immediately welcomed the figures as proof that his economic policy was working.

But he coupled the jubilation with a sharp call on Italian commercial banks to lower their lending rates to most customers, saying the fall in inflation was not enough in itself to guarantee economic recovery.
He said there was a growing gulf between interest rates banks applied to some clients and those which the majority of companies, particularly smaller businesses, paid.
"The rates range from eight percent for certain loans to rates of 16 to 18 percent for similar operations," Prodi said.
"The size of the margin is excessive and completely anomalous, not only compared with other countries, but also compared with the situation in the past," he said.
"It is therefore necessary that the whole range of bank interest rates should fall."
The Bank of Italy's key discount rate, which sets the trend for commercial rates, stands at 7.5 percent after a 0.75 percentage point cut on October 23, the second this year.

Economic analysts expect central bank governor Antonio Fazio, who has cautiously trimmed rates in response to evidence of lower inflation, to order a further slight cut later this month, probably of half a percentage point.
"The inflation figure was bang in line with expectations and showed that an interest rate cut is now long overdue," said a trader on the London International Financial Futures Exchange.
Prodi has set 2.5 percent as the average inflation target for 1997. He said recently that while inflation was now under control, any further falls would be only "very slight".
